node-1.label: Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy

node-2.label: Patient has high myopia with axial length measured as 30.0 mm

why.why: Radiologist analysis of OCT showing focal scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration and autofluorescence homogeneous low signal at the pit, together with axial length 30.0 mm and no mass, confirms myopic chorioretinal atrophy. This multimodal imaging evidence strongly supports the diagnosis, so confidence is raised from 0.75 to 0.92.

High myopia is not a typical cause of primary inflammation, and the radiologist explicitly notes that inflammatory chorioretinitis remains unsupported. OCT and autofluorescence findings are consistent with degenerative myopic atrophy rather than active inflammation, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.05.

Radiologist analysis shows no mass on OCT and describes scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration, effectively excluding choroidal tumor/mass. The unusual yellowish lesion is fully explained by myopic chorioretinal atrophy with scleral ectasia, so confidence is reduced from 0.10 to 0.02.
